name: Raga Lalit
shortDescription: A pre-dawn raga of suspended stillness and inner tension.
description: Raga Lalit opens in the hour before sunrise, carrying a contemplative and unresolved mood. It works best when the world is quiet and the mind is not yet fully awake. Its emotional world is one of yearning held in stillness — not resolved, but deeply felt.

name: Raga Bhairav
shortDescription: A dawn raga of gravity, devotion, and inner steadiness.
description: Raga Bhairav carries a solemn, devotional force. It is ideal for still morning listening and for creating a sense of sacred calm at the start of the day. Its gravity does not press — it steadies.

name: Raga Todi
shortDescription: A morning raga of intensity, yearning, and inward pull.
description: Raga Todi carries a searching and deeply introspective character. It suits quiet morning hours when the listener wants depth rather than comfort.

name: Raga Ahir Bhairav
shortDescription: A softer dawn raga with warmth, stillness, and quiet gravity.
description: Ahir Bhairav balances morning seriousness with a more tender and pastoral feeling. It is ideal for gentle awakening and unhurried stillness — devotional without being austere.

name: Raga Ramkali
shortDescription: Austere and reflective, with a disciplined morning atmosphere.
description: Raga Ramkali evokes austerity, clarity, and spiritual discipline. It is suited to reflective mornings and more inward listening — a raga that demands stillness in return for its depth.

name: Raga Bilaskhani Todi
shortDescription: A grave and moving morning raga with deep inward pull.
description: Bilaskhani Todi carries a mournful, searching quality. It fits listeners looking for emotional depth rather than brightness — a raga of quiet grief that settles into acceptance.

name: Raga Miyan ki Todi
shortDescription: A more intense and architecturally weighty morning Todi.
description: Miyan ki Todi brings a sharper, more dramatic inwardness. It suits listeners who want a profound and uncompromising meditative mood — austere, focused, and without ornament.

name: Raga Jaunpuri
shortDescription: A raga of tenderness, pathos, and restrained emotional release.
description: Jaunpuri carries sadness without heaviness. It can hold reflective listening, soft work, or inward emotional settling. A raga that does not demand attention — it simply accompanies.

name: Raga Asavari
shortDescription: Detached, inward, and gently severe.
description: Asavari has a stripped, restrained emotional quality. It works when the listener wants space rather than sentiment — a raga of elegant withdrawal.

name: Raga Brindavani Sarang
shortDescription: Bright yet gentle, with openness and devotional ease.
description: Brindavani Sarang is airy and uncluttered, making it useful for lightness and a calm afternoon reset. It carries a natural, devotional brightness without becoming decorative.

name: Raga Madhmad Sarang
shortDescription: Soft brightness without strain, good for easeful afternoons.
description: Madhmad Sarang offers lightness and balance without becoming decorative. It suits clear but unforced attention — the right raga for unhurried afternoon hours.

name: Raga Bhimpalasi
shortDescription: Warm, inward, and gently yearning — good for focused work.
description: Bhimpalasi balances introspection with ease. It is especially suited to afternoon attention, quiet study, and unhurried creative work — a raga that deepens concentration without demanding it.

name: Raga Multani
shortDescription: A late-afternoon raga with dry depth and inward heat.
description: Multani feels sun-soaked, inward, and patient. It rewards slow listening and creates a meditative sense of suspended time — the feeling of late afternoon pressing gently inward.

name: Raga Patdeep
shortDescription: Tender and reflective, with a soft emotional pull.
description: Patdeep is lyrical and emotive without becoming heavy. It is useful when the listener wants warmth, inwardness, and quiet emotional clarity as the afternoon softens toward evening.

name: Raga Yaman
shortDescription: Open, luminous, and expansive — an evening raga of grace.
description: Yaman is spacious and luminous, with an expansive emotional character. It is one of the most welcoming evening ragas and works beautifully for calm focus, unhurried reading, or a serene transition out of the day.

name: Raga Puriya
shortDescription: A sunset raga of intensity, suspension, and inward longing.
description: Puriya carries a charged stillness that feels particularly suited to the transition out of day. It works for deep unwinding and serious listening — emotionally intense, but resolving.

name: Raga Marwa
shortDescription: Unsettled, searching, and emotionally charged.
description: Marwa is one of the most psychologically tense ragas of the twilight hour. It is not comforting, but it is profoundly absorbing — a raga that holds the listener in productive unrest.

name: Raga Shree
shortDescription: Grave, expansive, and meditative at the edge of evening.
description: Raga Shree combines dignity with introspection, giving sunset listening a sacred and inward quality. It arrives like the last light — majestic and unhurried.

name: Raga Poorvi
shortDescription: A serious evening raga with introspective gravity.
description: Poorvi is measured, grave, and meditative. It suits listeners who want stillness with a sense of inward architecture — a raga that holds space rather than filling it.

name: Raga Desh
shortDescription: Lyrical and open-hearted, with freshness rather than weight.
description: Desh is welcoming and melodic, often carrying tenderness and uplift without losing inwardness. An accessible evening raga that softens the day without heaviness.

name: Raga Kedar
shortDescription: A night raga of peace, devotion, and luminous balance.
description: Kedar is serene and devotional, with enough spaciousness to support both meditation and calm evening unwinding. Its devotional character does not press — it simply illuminates.

name: Raga Bihag
shortDescription: Graceful and lyrical, with softness rather than heaviness.
description: Bihag offers ease and elegance, making it especially useful for relaxed focus and calm nighttime listening. A raga that asks nothing of the listener except presence.

name: Raga Hameer
shortDescription: Radiant and expansive, with celebratory grace.
description: Hameer is luminous and elevated, useful when the listener wants elegance and breadth rather than introspective weight. A night raga of unusual brightness and poise.

name: Raga Bageshree
shortDescription: Intimate, yearning, and ideal for late-night quiet.
description: Bageshree carries tenderness and late-night inwardness. It works especially well when the goal is emotional settling and sleep readiness — a raga of quiet, inward longing.

name: Raga Chandrakauns
shortDescription: A nocturnal raga of moonlit inwardness and mystery.
description: Chandrakauns feels sparse, suspended, and luminous in darkness. It suits deeply inward and quiet listening states — a raga that illuminates without disturbing.

name: Raga Darbari
shortDescription: Profound, grave, and one of the strongest night ragas for deep rest.
description: Darbari carries depth, weight, and profound stillness. It is ideal for late-night listening, deep rest, and easing the mind into sleep. One of the most revered and powerful ragas in the entire Hindustani tradition.

name: Raga Malkauns
shortDescription: A deep-night raga of elemental depth and dark stillness.
description: Malkauns is slow-burning, hypnotic, and powerful. It is one of the strongest ragas for deep-night inwardness and profound quiet — a raga that does not ask permission to go deep.

name: Raga Adana
shortDescription: Late-night energy and force — sharper and more alert than Darbari.
description: Adana introduces a more vigorous, alert late-night mood. Unlike the heavy gravity of Darbari, Adana is energised and forceful. Best used when the listener wants focused attention rather than rest.

name: Raga Shankara
shortDescription: Poised, stately, and more upright than deeply sleepy.
description: Shankara offers majesty without heaviness, making it a useful entry point for late-night listening that does not pull toward sleep — elegant, alert, and architecturally rich.

name: Raga Bhairavi
shortDescription: A timeless raga of farewell, devotion, and emotional release.
description: Bhairavi carries surrender, pathos, and a rare ability to dissolve emotional tension. It is one of the broadest and most versatile entry points in the entire library — heard at any hour, in any mood, it finds you.

name: Raga Kafi
shortDescription: Grounded, natural, and ideal for sustained concentration.
description: Kafi allows attention to settle without strain. It is one of the strongest all-day ragas for focus, reading, and gentle concentration — natural, earthy, and entirely without artifice.

name: Raga Malwa
